subject: Post-demo: grounding metrics + retriever/reranker config for Atlas AI
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moroz <elena@atlasai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + suggested eval scope from today's demo

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate you and Tom carving out the time. Per our conversation I wanted to summarize the recommended next steps for a lightweight RAG evaluation so we can quickly validate model fit and grounding risk before we scope a pilot. I kept this narrow so we can get initial results in ~1 week.

Quick recap of goals you mentioned:
- Highly factual answers to regulatory Qs (accurate citations to your policy corpus)
- Low hallucination rate for customer-facing explanation flows
- SLA-like bounds on time-to-first-token (ideally < 350ms P50) for single-turn lookups

Proposed minimal eval (deliverables):
1) Retrieval configurations to try (3 variants):
  - Dense-only (embedding size 1536, cosine) + no reranker (baseline)
  - Dense + lexical hybrid (BM25 boost) + light reranker (cross-encoder distilled)
  - Dense + heavier reranker (full cross-encoder) + prefix caching enabled
2) Model matrix to benchmark (shortlist):
  - LLaMA2-13B-q4 (fast baseline), Redstone-7B-finetuned (higher factuality), Open-Chat-16B (best quality check)
3) Prompt sets: 120 queries across 3 buckets (regulatory, support, policy-interpretation). I attached the draft prompt-set-v2 for review.
4) Metrics we suggest reporting: grounding precision@k (P@1,P@3), faithfulness error rate (human adjudication on 50 samples), and a simple QA regressed-diff vs baseline (to catch quality regressions).

Attachments I'm pushing to the shared Drive: prompt-sets-v2.jsonl, retriever-config.yaml, and a quick benchmark CSV template. Links below as well.

Asks / decisions from you:
- Confirm the three retrieval variants are fine or suggest swapping one for an LLM-only fallback test.
- Approve the 120 query seed (we can augment later).
- Permission to run a short synthetic load (500 concurrent small requests) to validate latency numbers on your Dedicated trial region.

If you say go, Aditya and I will spin the jobs and aim to have the first report by next Friday (6/18).

Best,
Soojin

-- 
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments: prompt-sets-v2.jsonl (jsonl, 120 prompts); retriever-config.yaml (text); atlas-rag-benchmarks-v1.csv (template)

From: Elena Moroz <elena@atlasai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + suggested eval scope from today's demo

Hi Soojin — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifying notes from our side after talking to product: 

- For the model shortlist, can you add one quantized-16 variant of the 13B so we can see cost/latency tradeoffs (q8/q4/16 ideal)?
- On metrics: how do you compute "grounding precision@k" precisely? We need that definition for our compliance folks.
- We have a small corpus of PDFs with embedded tables — retrieval performance there has been spotty. Please include a retrieval variant that uses chunking+table-aware embeddings if that's feasible.

We are OK with the 120 queries but will label 20 of them as high-sensitivity — we want those prioritized in the adjudication set. Tom is copied to coordinate procurement for the Dedicated trial.

Elena

--
Elena Moroz
Head of Product, Atlas AI
elena@atlasai.com

On Thu, Jun 10, 2027 at 09:40 AM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again, will adjust.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moroz <elena@atlasai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + suggested eval scope from today's demo

Elena / Tom —

Great, a few concrete updates based on your asks:
1) Model matrix now includes: LLaMA2-13B (q4, q8, q16 simulated), Redstone-7B-finetuned, Open-Chat-16B. We'll label latency/cost per-token for each quantization level.
2) Grounding precision@k definition (brief): fraction of queries where at least one retrieved passage among top-k contains a supporting citation that the model cites verbatim in its answer. We'll include a short adjudication rubric in the Drive so your compliance reviewers can see how we mark supporting evidence.
3) PDF/table handling: added a retrieval variant that applies chunking with table-aware tokenization + embeddings tuned on table rows. Config saved in retriever-config.yaml.
4) High-sensitivity bucket: noted 20 queries — those will get double-blind human adjudication.

I uploaded three attachments to the shared Drive and pasted the links below. The benchmark job will run on a small Dedicated node (your trial) — Tom, can you confirm the trial region and whether we have a temporary service account so Redwood can spin jobs? If you prefer, we can run the initial quality runs on our hosted infra and share results immediately, but latency numbers won't reflect your Dedicated SLA.

Next steps:
- Tom: confirm Dedicated trial region and service account OR grant permission to run on Redwood hosted infra (we'll mark latency as "hosted estimate").
- Elena: sign-off on the 120 queries and the 20 high-sensitivity seeds.
- Aditya / Marissa (internal): once Tom confirms, we'll queue three retrieval variants x 3 models x 120 queries (~1,080 runs). Aditya, can you pick the exact cross-encoder reranker version (distilled or full) you want to try first? Distilled gives faster rerank but might miss fine-grain grounding.

I'll kick off prep once we have those decisions — expect progress updates in this thread plus a short summary doc after first-run artifacts are in.

Thanks,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AtlasDemoShared; CI benchmark run template: https://ci.redwood.ai/reports/atl-benchmark-2027-06-09

From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@atlasai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Elena Moroz <elena@atlasai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + suggested eval scope from today's demo

Soojin / team —

We can confirm the Dedicated trial in us-west-2 and I created a project service account you can use (tom-atlas-trial-sa@atlasai-gcp.iam.gserviceaccount.com). I'll share the key in the procurement ticket (not in email). Please proceed and run the hosted baseline first and then a short Dedicated run when you have the service account.

Also, for the reranker: start with the distilled cross-encoder (you mentioned a 2-stage approach) and if we see grounding recall gaps we'll flip to the full cross-encoder for the high-sensitivity bucket.

Elena: we sign off on the 120 queries and the 20 high-sensitivity samples.

Tom

--
Tom Hayes
VP Engineering, Atlas AI
